en.title: Empty Lots Close Enough to All Houses
en.description:
In the grid, 0 is an empty lot and 1 is a house. A store can be built on an empty lot whose Manhattan distance to every house is at most K. Find the number of suitable empty lots; if there are no houses, every empty lot qualifies.

The input protocol, the ranges added by this site, the examples, and the tests were written independently by CSWork.
en.input: This site's input: the first line contains R C K (1≤R,C≤500, 0≤K≤1000), followed by R lines each with C values 0 or 1.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation:
Example 1: only the two empty lots to the right of and below the house are at distance 1; the bottom-right corner is at distance 2 and does not qualify, so the answer is 2.

Example 2: there are no houses, and the only empty lot satisfies every constraint, so the answer is 1.

Example 3: there are only houses and no empty lots, so the answer is 0.
hints: Maintain the minimum and maximum of x+y and x−y over all houses; for each empty lot, check whether its differences from all four extremes are ≤K.
